methods.name: Momentum scaled by its own realized volatility
methods.sourceRef: Barroso & Santa-Clara (2015), Momentum has its moments, JFE 116(1); Daniel & Moskowitz (2016), Momentum crashes, JFE 122(2)
methods.hypothesis: F4-MOM12-N20-TREND beat SPY TR (CAGR +16.2% vs +7.9%, PF 2.27) and failed only on max DD (22.2%). Scaling its book by target_vol over its own 3-month realized volatility cuts exposure in exactly the high-vol spells where momentum crashes, so max DD falls under 15% while CAGR stays above SPY's.
methods.expectedFailure: Monthly rebalancing reacts too slowly: a fast crash (Oct 2008, Aug 2011) does its damage inside one month before the scale updates, leaving max DD at 16-20%; or the 10% target cuts CAGR below SPY TR.
methods.analysis:
### 2026-10-04

**Result (dev window 1996-01-03 → 2015-10-16, N = 58).** No variant is eligible, but this is the first lab or P7a trial to pass max DD ≤ 15%, PF ≥ 1.3 and ≥ 100 trades together. Every variant failed the same remaining condition: it did not beat total-return SPY (+351.4%, CAGR ≈ +7.9%).

| Variant | Return | CAGR | Max DD | PF | Trades | DSR | Failed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TV10 (monthly) | +224.9% | +6.1% | 11.0% | 2.31 | 1,109 | 0.903 | beats SPY, DSR |
| TV12 (monthly) | +327.6% | +7.6% | 12.9% | 2.27 | 1,130 | 0.899 | beats SPY, DSR |
| TV10-W (weekly) | +129.7% | +4.3% | 10.6% | 1.49 | 2,602 | 0.703 | beats SPY, DSR |
| TV10-NOTREND | +198.4% | +5.7% | 18.0% | 1.77 | 1,411 | 0.758 | beats SPY, max DD, DSR |

**Hypothesis: half right.** Own-volatility scaling did fix the drawdown. F4-MOM12-N20-TREND's 22.2% fell to 11–13%, and 2008 is no longer the worst year for the trend-filtered variants (their worst year is 2015, at −2.3%). The return was cut too, from CAGR +16.2% to +6.1–7.6%. The second half of the expected failure ("the 10% target cuts CAGR below SPY TR") is what happened. The first half (a monthly scale too slow for a fast crash) did not: max DD stayed under 13%.

**Why.** A top-20 momentum book runs at roughly 20–25% annualized volatility, so a 10–12% target holds it at about half exposure most of the time, not only in crash spells. Combined with the SPY 200-day filter (cash in bear markets), the book is de-risked twice. The scale is capped at 1 (no leverage), so calm spells never make up the lost exposure. The return/drawdown trade is close to linear: TV10 → TV12 added +1.5 pts CAGR for +1.9 pts DD. Extrapolating, a target around 14% should land near SPY's CAGR with DD around 15%, which is right on the edge of the gate.

**Weekly re-ranking hurt.** TV10-W more than doubled trades (2,602), cut PF to 1.49 and CAGR to +4.3%. Faster re-scaling buys no drawdown (10.6% vs 11.0%) and pays for it in turnover and whipsaw. **The trend filter matters:** without it (TV10-NOTREND), own-vol scaling alone lets 2008 through (−13.8%, DD 18.0%). In this setup Barroso's scaling is not a substitute for the regime filter.

**DSR.** 0.90 for the monthly variants at N = 58, under 0.95 even before the SPY condition. The Sharpe (0.81) is good but not exceptional after deflation.

**What it teaches.** The frontier is now known to pass through DD ≈ 13% at CAGR ≈ SPY. Beating SPY at DD ≤ 15% needs either more return per unit of risk (a better signal), or a scale that de-risks only in crash regimes instead of all the time.
methods.verdict: Own-vol scaling fixed max DD (11-13%, PF 2.3, 1.1k trades) but cut CAGR to 6-7.6% vs SPY TR ~7.9%: fails only 'beats SPY' (and DSR 0.90)

methods.name: Momentum, own-vol scaling only in high-vol regimes (asymmetric scale)
methods.hypothesis: M0001 de-risked all the time (a 10-12% target on a ~22% vol book means about half exposure always). Scaling down only when the book's own 3-month vol is above its long-run median, and staying fully invested otherwise, should keep F4's +16% CAGR in calm spells and still cut the crash spells, landing at DD <= 15% with CAGR above SPY TR.

methods.name: Dynamic momentum (Daniel-Moskowitz): weight by forecast mean / variance
methods.hypothesis: Momentum crashes happen in bear-market rebounds when volatility is high. Weighting by forecast return (low after a bear market) over forecast variance, instead of by variance alone, de-risks only in the dangerous state and keeps exposure elsewhere, giving more return per unit of drawdown than M0001's plain vol target.

insights.title: Volatility scaling buys drawdown at a near-linear price in return
insights.body: Scaling top-20 momentum to a 10-12% own-volatility target cut max DD from 22% to 11-13% but also CAGR from 16% to 6-7.6%, because a ~22%-vol book is held at about half exposure all the time, not just in crashes. The frontier passes near DD 13% at SPY's CAGR. To beat SPY under DD 15% we need more return per unit of risk, or de-risking that triggers only in dangerous regimes.

insights.title: Delisted stocks and fundamentals
insights.body: The store has no delisted names (survivorship makes stock results optimistic) and no fundamentals, so value, quality, profitability and earnings-surprise strategies, the best-documented factors after momentum, cannot be tested. A point-in-time source such as Sharadar or a CRSP/Compustat-like feed would unlock them and make every stock result more honest.

insights.title: The 15% max-DD bar over 1996-2015 includes two -50% crashes
insights.body: The dev window contains the 2000-02 and 2008-09 bear markets. Any strategy with meaningful equity exposure must sidestep most of both to stay under 15%, so the gate rewards crash avoidance above everything else. Expect winners to be regime-switching or heavily de-risked designs, and expect their test-window (2015-2026, one sharp 2020 crash) behaviour to differ.

insights.title: Weekly risk checks with monthly re-ranking
insights.body: M0001's weekly variant re-ranked and re-scaled together, which more than doubled turnover and cut PF to 1.49. A rule set that re-ranks monthly but re-scales exposure weekly would test whether faster risk control helps without the whipsaw cost. That needs a new TradeRules cadence split (rank cadence vs resize cadence).
